references.text: The Lord predicts that he will strike Egypt with all his wondrous deeds, and that Pharaoh will then let the people go.
The Lord tells Moses that Pharaoh must let the people of Israel leave with a strong hand, and even drive them out of his land.
Fulfillment of the prophecy: Pharaoh calls for Moses and Aaron during the night and orders them to leave, and the Egyptians urge the people to depart from the land in haste.
The final plague that the Lord warned about: All the firstborn in Egypt die, causing great mourning throughout the land.
The Lord predicts that he will lay his hand on Egypt with great judgments and lead out the army of Israel.
Stephen speaks of Moses who led the people out after performing signs and wonders in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
By faith Moses kept the Passover and sprinkled blood on the doorposts so that the destroyer would not touch their firstborn.
Exodus 4:21 explains the reason for the duration of the conflict, while Exodus 11:1 shows God's final breakthrough against this hardness.
